discoveries:
- Row W2-L423's rule takes a 40-hex value only when a space, quote, `;`, literal `\n`/`\r` or the end follows it.
- git 2.43 resolves 39- and 12-digit prefixes, upper case and annotated tags under `^{commit}`. That is why the code checks for exactly 40 digits and accepts only an object whose own type is commit.
- The reviewer found that git's lazy fetch in a partial clone sends unknown candidate matches to the promisor remote (F1). This is new with this ticket. git 2.43 has no switch to stop it.
- Row W2-L423 was still open when picked up (DEC-718); this ticket fixes it at a63e012f6745.
risks:
- F1: in a partial clone, a candidate match that may be a real token is sent to the promisor remote, although the verdict still fails closed. This programme's repository is a full clone, so it does not occur here today.
- F3: the record form did not change, so the pinned judge reuses clean results this code wrote. That passes stores that hold only real commit hashes; no credential can pass this way.
- If the merge brings in another conftest or configuration change, the DEC-919 case stays red.
lessons:
- Write a rule's keywords as `"".join((...))`. Python folds `"a" + "b"` into one constant in the compiled file.
- An exempt finding must not end the scan early: every rule set still runs (DEC-347).
- W2-69's suite takes about 35 minutes sandboxed, and its daemon cases need a writable `/tmp/gov-cbm`.
- The guard refuses variables in write targets and `bash -c` scripts it cannot check. Use literal paths and plain commands.
